title: SLA-driven intake & prioritization matrix for third-party provisioning & org-admin requests
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers are submitting disparate admin/access requests that span RBAC role design, SAML IdP integrations, SCIM provisioning for third-party identity providers, and org policy exceptions. Current intake is unstructured and causes long response times, incorrect prioritization, and repeated engineering rework.

Scope: Design a repeatable intake form, an SLA-driven prioritization matrix, and clear triage heuristics that the Solutions, Support, and Sales teams can apply for non-bug admin/access requests (RBAC, SSO/SAML, SCIM, org policy overrides, service-account provisioning). Output must include: intake form fields, decision matrix with SLAs, escalation paths, and a minimal rollout plan for the Console and internal playbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Consolidated intake form (Console + Zendesk template) covering identity metadata, customer impact, compliance context, and desired timeline
Prioritization matrix that maps request types to SLA buckets (P0/P1/P2) and owners (Security/Platform/Support)
Triage playbook with gating rules to reject/collect more info/accept and route
Documentation pages for Sales and Support with 3 example request flows (RBAC role request, SAML integration, SCIM connector onboarding)
Pilot run with 3 enterprise customers and metrics captured: time-to-triage, time-to-resolution, and rework rate
proposal_summary: Create an SLA-driven prioritization matrix that classifies admin/access requests along two axes: customer risk (compliance, data access) and engineering cost/complexity. Each cell maps to an SLA (Triage within 4h / 24h / 72h) and a routing owner. Complement with a structured intake form that forces required artifacts (SAML metadata, SCIM schema, role entitlements) and a lightweight automated validation on submission to reduce back-and-forth. Provide runbook snippets for Support and Solutions for common patterns and a Console UI stub for the intake flow.
triage_rubric:
Classification axes:
- Risk: none | low | medium | high (based on data domain, privileged scopes, regulatory needs)
- Complexity: trivial | integration | custom engineering | infra changes

SLA mapping (examples):
- High risk + infra change -> P0 -> Triage within 4h, Security + ENG oncall, target resolution 7d
- Medium risk + integration -> P1 -> Triage within 24h, Solutions + ENG owner, target resolution 14d
- Low risk + trivial -> P2 -> Triage within 72h, Support owner, target resolution 30d

Gating rules (auto-reject or require more info):
- Missing SAML metadata for IdP requests -> send automated checklist
- SCIM onboarding without SCIM base URL or admin token -> mark as incomplete
- RBAC requests that request owner-level access for >3 users -> escalate to Security review
intake_form_fields:
Required fields for every submission:
- Customer name and account ID
- Contact and technical lead (name, email, phone)
- Request type (RBAC | SSO/SAML | SCIM | Org policy exception | Service account)
- Business justification and SLA requested
- Security/compliance context (PCI/DPA/HIPAA/other)
- Artifacts: SAML metadata file or URL, SCIM schema sample, list of roles and entitlements, screenshots of current Console state
- Desired timeline and go-live date
- Affected environments (prod/staging/dev)
- Attachments (max 25MB)

Optional automated checks on submit:
- Validate SAML metadata XML schema, warn on missing NameID formats
- Ping SCIM base URL, validate 200/401 response, and record allowed methods
- Check for entitlements that map to 'admin' or 'owner' and flag for security review
routing_and_escalation:
Owners by category:
- SSO/SAML (IdP integrations with org-wide impact) -> Solutions + Security review
- SCIM connectors (third-party provisioning) -> Platform + ENG Integration owner
- RBAC role design and org policy exceptions -> Security + Product (Console permissions)
- Service accounts & automation -> Platform Engineering

Escalation path:
1) Triage owner assigns engineer or solutions lead within SLA
2) If unresolved at 50% of target resolution time, escalate to product manager for decision
3) If unresolved at 90% of target resolution time or high-customer-impact, engage CSM and schedule weekly sync till resolution
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (2 weeks): Draft intake form and triage rubric; prepare internal docs and Slack shortcuts; wireframe Console intake page.
Phase 2 (4 weeks): Implement Zendesk template + lightweight backend validation; train Support and Solutions on playbook; pilot with 3 enterprise customers.
Phase 3 (6 weeks): Iterate on rubric from pilot feedback; build Console intake UI and automated checks; add telemetry for metrics.
Phase 4 (ongoing): Bake into readiness checklist for Dedicated/Private deployments and integrate with runbooks for on-call teams.
metrics_and_success_criteria: Time to triage (median) falls to <= 24h for P1 requests
Time to resolution for P1 <= 14 days for integration requests
Reduction in back-and-forth clarifying questions by 40% (measured by ticket comments)
Pilot feedback NPS >= 70 from Solutions/CSM on intake quality
Reduction in emergency security reviews due to mis-scoped RBAC requests
notes_and_discussion:
03/10 - Kickoff: Aligned with Sales and Support on top pain points: missing SAML artifacts, vague RBAC asks, and SCIM connectors that require custom mapping.
03/12 - Security review with Priya: agreed that any request granting owner-level access must be auto-flagged; will draft a template risk statement.
03/15 - Engineering input from ENG:4021 suggests adding a pre-flight SCIM probe to validate endpoints; flagged estimate impact.
03/16 - Decided to pilot with 3 customers: two existing enterprise accounts doing SCIM onboarding and one new SAML migration.
Outstanding decisions: whether to auto-approve SCIM connectors for customers who present vendor-signed security attestations, and whether to expose intake progress in Console or keep internal first.
reviews:
PM review by Maya Chen 03/11: approved concept and pilot.
Security review by Priya Rao 03/12: required owner-access auto-flag.
Engineering feasibility by Oliver Grant 03/15: recommended adding automated SCIM probe and small schema validator (ENG-4021).
decision_log:

03/15: Include automated SCIM base-URL probe in pilot but gate full production rollout on ENG capacity.
03/16: Pilot customers selected and CSMs notified.
